issues.legal_issue: Civil courts lack jurisdiction over a suit seeking to determine succession to a jagir when recognition of succession is reserved exclusively to a sovereign authority.
material_facts: The suit sought a declaration of entitlement to succeed to a jagir and disputed the alleged adopted heir’s succession.
The pleadings described earlier successions to the jagir as having been sanctioned by the ruler in the exercise of sovereign authority.
The pleadings did not allege that the jagir was hereditary or that the ruler’s sanction was merely formal, and no evidence established that it was hereditary.
A covenant vested exclusively in the successor sovereign authority the right to recognise succession to jagirdars’ rights and titles.
The successor sovereign authority had recognised the alleged adopted heir as successor.
issues.conclusion: The civil courts’ jurisdiction to entertain the suit was impliedly barred, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure gives civil courts jurisdiction over suits of a civil nature unless their cognizance is expressly or impliedly barred. Although a dispute over property or office is generally civil, a question of succession to a jagir reserved exclusively for determination by a sovereign authority on political considerations is not for a civil court to adjudicate. Under Gulabdas Jugjivandas v Collector of Surat, 3 Bom 186, a jagir is prima facie a life estate absent evidence that it was granted as hereditary; and Sultan Sani v Ajmodin, 20 Ind App 50 (PC), establishes that the grant of a saranjam or jagir upon its holder’s death is exclusively for the Government to decide and is not reviewable by a legal tribunal. The covenant’s Article VII(3) placed recognition of succession exclusively with the successor sovereign authority.

predicates.civil_suit_challenges_jagir_succession: A claimant brought a civil suit disputing who succeeds to a jagir.
predicates.succession_recognition_reserved_to_sover: The governing arrangement assigned exclusive authority to a sovereign body to recognise succession to the jagir.

issues.definition: When a civil suit disputes succession to a jagir and the governing arrangement reserves recognition of that succession exclusively to a sovereign body, civil jurisdiction is impliedly barred.
